source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §4 Some Winning Positions in the Middle-game, Example 16

narration.say: The same type of combination, in a more complicated form.
The bishop on d3 aims at h7, but the knight on f5 is in the way.

steps.title: Clearing the line
steps.source: 1 Kt x Kt ch (this clears the line for the B); B x Kt (to stop the Kt from moving to Kt 5 after the sacrifice of the B).

narration.say: Knight takes on e7, check. This clears the line for the bishop.
Bishop takes back. It will stop the other knight from going to g5 later.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Remove the bishop that guards g5.

feedback.*: The rook on e2 can take the bishop.

exercise.success: 2. Rxe7. Black's best is to take with the knight.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Sacrifice the bishop.

feedback.*: The bishop takes on h7 with check.

narration.say: The queen comes in, with check.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check with the queen.

feedback.*: The queen checks on the h-file.

exercise.success: 4. Qh5, check. Black goes to g8.

narration.say: And the knight joins, threatening mate on h7.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Threaten mate on h7.

feedback.*: The knight supports the queen on h7.

exercise.success: 5. Ng5. Black moves his rook to c8, to make room for the king on f8.

narration.say: Queen to h7, check. The king runs to f8.
Queen to h8, check. The knight blocks on g8.
Knight to h7, check. The king goes to e7.
Rook to e1, check. The king goes to d8.

exercise.prompt: White to move and give checkmate in one.

feedback.*: The queen can take a piece with mate.

exercise.hint: The queen takes the knight on g8.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: It will be seen that all the combinations shown have for a foundation the proper co-ordination of the pieces, which have all been brought to bear against a weak point.

narration.say: This combination is long, and a beginner could hardly calculate it all.
But knowing the type of combination, you might find a brilliant attack you would otherwise never think of.
All these combinations rest on the co-ordination of the pieces against a weak point.
